description: issue #682 (slice I3): a handler block is NOT a procedure body, so `return`/`stop` inside it are `return`/`stop` OUTSIDE a procedure — even when the `when` was registered inside one. Here `when "start"` is registered inside `define setup`; the `"start"` handler fires immediately (the run has started) and hits `return 5`. Without a boundary conversion the `return` signal would escape into `setup`'s call frame and be silently consumed as `setup`'s own return; instead the handler boundary converts it to `ol-return-outside-proc` (spec/error-model.md), pointing at the `return` keyword. The escape is decided statically now, so the program does not run and no `return` trace event is emitted; under the `runUnchecked` opt-out the statement still emits one before the boundary reclassifies the escaping signal. Issue #815: `execute()` now runs Layer 1 and Layer 2 before Phase 2 and refuses a program carrying an `error`-severity finding (`spec/execution-model.md:659-664`), so no event is emitted and the diagnostic delivered here is the CHECK's. The runtime's own copy of the rule still exists, but it runs only under the `runUnchecked` opt-out — NOT in this fixture, which is checked — and when it does run it is collapsed into the check's by the de-duplication rule (`spec/execution-model.md:741-748`), which is why the runtime's copy never appears beside the check's. So nothing here observes that copy, and reading this fixture as evidence for it would be a mistake: measured, a runtime guard can be deleted outright with the whole conformance corpus still green, because the surviving report is the check's either way. What the runtime copy uniquely contributes is that the run STOPS at the fault, which is written in the event stream rather than in the diagnostics and is pinned by `packages/runtime/src/runtime-guards-halt.test.mjs`.
